newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil suspends payment on special farm debt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil suspends payment on special farm debt.

text.p: The Brazilian Finance Ministry Friday suspended renegotiations of a some $1.6 billion in special farm debt while it investigated suspicions of a leak of sensitive information, the ministry said.

The ministry said in a statement that "in order to protect the national interest" it had asked the National Treasury to hold up payments to holders of so-called Agrarian Debt Paper (TDA) until rumors about a leak had been cleared.
Earlier this week, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed a decree allowing TDAs to be exchanged for other Treasury paper.
The decree allows the government to pay cash for 10 percent of the face value of TDAs, with the remaining 90 percent to be exchanged for new TDAs issued by the Treasury, so-called TDA-Es.
The deal, contained in a decree hiking taxes on unproductive farm land, applies to TDA's issued by the federal land reform agency INCRA up to June 22, 1992, which trade at great discount.
TDA's were used to pay for disappropriated land. Since June 24, 1992, the Treasury has assumed responsibility for the process and issued TDA-Es.
